weakness.title: Missing Physical Entry Control for Sensitive Area
weakness.description: The facility does not control entry to an area that holds sensitive assets, so anyone who can reach the area can enter it.

extended_description.applicability: Rooms, enclosures and zones whose contents justify restricting entry, such as server rooms, network closets, archives and rooms holding confidential material. Areas that hold nothing sensitive, or that are intentionally open to the public, are not affected. A control that is present but too weak or bypassable is not covered by this entry.
extended_description.exploitation: Any person who can reach the door or opening of the area can enter it, with no check of identity or authorization.

row.details: Unauthorized persons can view, copy or remove information, media and equipment.
Equipment can be tampered with, reconfigured or connected to.
Equipment can be switched off, damaged or removed.

row.description: Fit each sensitive area with a control suited to its sensitivity, such as an electronic lock with a reader, a keyed lock with managed keys, or an attended checkpoint.

row.measure: Close and lock the door automatically
row.description: Use a door that closes and locks by itself, so that the control is not left open by default.
Authorize named persons or roles for the area, and withdraw access when it is no longer needed.
Log entries to the area and review the records.
The control must not impede exit. Where regulations require it, the door must open from the inside without a key or credential.
The state of electronic locks on power loss must be defined with evacuation in mind.
Responders must be able to enter through a documented procedure.

row.reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: PE-3 Physical Access Control
ISO/IEC 27001:2022, Annex A: 7.2 Physical entry, 7.3 Securing offices, rooms and facilities
